summary: Booking.com is website and mobile apps for booking accommodation, founded in 1996. Type: part of a foreign group (BOOKING HOLDINGS INC., US). About 17,500 employees (Wikidata). Recognised visa sponsor (IND). 100% of its 10 jobs here don't ask for Dutch. News, last 3 months: 1 about funding; 1 about acquisitions; 1 about growth or hiring; 14 about legal trouble, strikes or bankruptcy.

insights.one_liner: Amsterdam-based travel booking platform and big international employer; all jobs in English, IND sponsor, but currently in a legal fight over office days.

culture.text: About 17,313 people on LinkedIn, mostly from UvA, VU, TU Delft, Manchester and Amsterdam UAS, studying computer science, business and economics.
Its 10 jobs are all in Amsterdam, spread over finance, consulting, software engineering and data, with 3 entry-level roles.
Staff quoted saying they hold all their meetings in Teams or Slack, so location shouldn't matter.

open.text: Booking.com B.V. and two other Booking entities are IND recognised sponsors.
None of its 10 jobs here require Dutch and 30% mention visa or relocation.
Jobs draw about 114 applicants each on LinkedIn on average.

growth.text: Founded in 1996, with about 17,500 employees, and owned by US-listed Booking Holdings.
Developed an internal platform for building modular AI agents.

worth_knowing.text: Booking.com and its works council went to court over mandatory office days for staff.
The judge appeared to side with Booking in the dispute over working from home.
